alerts.reason: Big Lots reported a 2.5% decline in annual comparable sales while year-end inventory rose 31.6% (B, C). That buildup suggests merchandise was selling more slowly than planned. If it takes another quarter to clear, markdowns could push consolidated net sales through the 5% decline threshold in the quarter beginning in May. The timing is uncertain because the sales clue is annual.

Barnes & Noble Education’s January-quarter sales fell 2.1% (A). It finalized the sale of its logo merchandise inventory in the prior-year counterpart of the May target quarter (C). If that finalization contributed to reported sales then, the tougher comparison could push the May-quarter decline to 5% or more after a shallower April-quarter decline. The filing gives no quarterly sales amount for the transaction.

GameStop’s quarterly net sales growth slowed from 29.05% to 6.21%. I expect growth to stay above -5% in the intervening quarter, then fall to -5% or lower in May–July. Higher-priced new consoles helped lift prior-year sales, and GameStop built inventory to mitigate supply disruptions that could limit repeat hardware sales (C, D).

Big Lots’ quarterly net sales change improved from -3.07% to -0.34%, supporting an intervening quarter above -5%. Annual comparable sales fell 2.5% while year-end inventory rose 31.6% (B, C). If that inventory requires markdowns, lower selling prices could push May–July net sales to a decline of at least 5%.

Abercrombie’s quarterly net sales growth slowed from 10.43% to 3.50%. Fiscal 2021 growth depended mainly on store traffic recovering from closures, while digital sales grew only 4% (A). I expect the intervening quarter to stay above -5%, then May–July sales to fall at least 5% as the company compares against recovered store traffic.
